ai.description: This lizard reaches 20 cm in length. It is brownish-green with dark lateral blotches and lacks a prominent dorsal crest. A distinctive black patch marks the shoulder area.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pseudocalotes andamanensis* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian agamids by the complete absence of a dorsal crest, featuring only a smooth, uniform nape.
ai.habitat: *Pseudocalotes andamanensis* inhabits the dense, humid tropical evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found in low-to-mid-altitude canopy vegetation.
ai.behavior: *Pseudocalotes andamanensis* is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks to ambush passing insects while relying on its cryptic coloration for defense.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudocalotes andamanensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from May to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Pseudocalotes andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, where it inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests at low elevations.
